title: Two-sided bar horizontal contraction and total augmentation
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal D$ be a small ordinary category, $R$ a commutative ring, $F:\mathcal D\to\operatorname{Mod}_R$ a covariant functor, and $Q:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D$ a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. For $p,q\geq0$ put
$$A_{p,q}=\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_p\xrightarrow f Q_q}F(T_0).$$
Horizontal faces delete $T_i$, applying $F(T_0\to T_1)$ when $i=0$ and composing with $f$ when $i=p$; vertical operators postcompose $f$ with the operators of $Q$. Let $\partial_h,\partial_v$ be the alternating face sums in positive respective indices, zero at index zero. Put $A_{p,q}$ in cochain bidegree $(-p,-q)$ and use finite-diagonal total differential $\partial_h+(-1)^p\partial_v$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Put $S^{-q}=F(Q_q)$ with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms. Put $B^{-p}=\bigoplus_{T_0\to\cdots\to T_p}F(T_0)$, zero in positive degrees, with alternating faces deleting $T_i$ and applying $F$ only at the first face. Complexes and their derived categories mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. These formulas define a commuting double complex. The map $e_Q:\operatorname{Tot}A\to S$, zero for $p>0$ and $(T\xrightarrow fQ_q,x)\mapsto F(f)x$ for $p=0$, and the map $e_B:\operatorname{Tot}A\to B$, zero for $q>0$ and forgetting $f:T_p\to Q_0$ for $q=0$, are chain maps.
For every fixed $q$, augment the horizontal chain complex by $F(Q_q)$ in augmented degree $-1$. The maps
$$h_{-1}(y)=(Q_q\xrightarrow1 Q_q,y),\qquad h_p(T_0\to\cdots\to T_p\xrightarrow fQ_q,x)=(-1)^{p+1}(T_0\to\cdots\to T_p\xrightarrow fQ_q\xrightarrow1Q_q,x)$$
for $p\geq0$ satisfy $\partial h+h\partial=1$, including augmented degree $-1$. The map $e_Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence $e_Q:\operatorname{Tot}A\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ in $D(R)$. The transpose total convention $\partial_v+(-1)^q\partial_h$ is identified with the chosen convention by multiplication by $(-1)^{pq}$ on $A_{p,q}$; this identification is the identity on the edge $p=0$ defining $e_Q$. These conclusions impose no contractibility hypothesis on any representable evaluation of $Q$.

proof.text: All sums are indexed by sets: smallness of $\mathcal D$ bounds both its strings and the arrows into $Q_q$. Define every operator by its $R$-linear map on a summand, and extend by the universal property of the direct sum. Thus each finitely supported vector has a finitely supported image. Write $d_i^h$ and $d_j^v$ for the horizontal and vertical faces. The identity $d_i^h d_j^h=d_{j-1}^h d_i^h$ for $i<j$ is deletion of the same two vertices. At adjacent deletions it is associativity of composition; when the first vertex is deleted it is $F(ba)=F(b)F(a)$, including the last-face composite into $Q_q$. The vertical identity $d_i^v d_j^v=d_{j-1}^v d_i^v$ follows from functoriality of $Q$ on the two equal injections in $\Delta$. Every horizontal face commutes with every vertical face: only the last arrow changes vertically, and $Q(\delta)(fa)=(Q(\delta)f)a$, while the first-face coefficient map is unchanged.

source.place: Tag 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution), explicit categorical two-sided-bar construction; agent verification of face formulas

proof.text: Pairing the two occurrences of each double deletion with opposite signs gives $\partial_h^2=\partial_v^2=0$; the same cancellation proves that $S$ and $B$ are complexes. The commuting-face identities give $\partial_h\partial_v=\partial_v\partial_h$. For the displayed total differential, its cross terms on $A_{p,q}$ are $(-1)^{p-1}\partial_v\partial_h$ and $(-1)^p\partial_h\partial_v$, which cancel. Terms leaving the axes are zero by convention. In cochain degree $-n$ the diagonal has just the $n+1$ possible pairs $(p,q)$ with $p+q=n$; in positive degrees it is zero. Therefore the finite direct sums and the differential in the statement define the asserted total complex. This is the signed formula of [def-sp-double-complex-total] applied to bidegrees $(-p,-q)$, with $(-1)^{-p}=(-1)^p$.

source.place: Tag 0132 (lemma-first-quadrant-ss), finite-diagonal setting; direct sign calculation, not an application of its spectral-sequence conclusion

proof.text: Let $\epsilon_q:A_{0,q}\to F(Q_q)$ be the sum of the maps $F(f)$. On a summand indexed by $T_0\xrightarrow aT_1\xrightarrow fQ_q$ the two terms of $\epsilon_q\partial_h$ are $F(f)F(a)x$ and $-F(fa)x$, so they cancel. Postcomposition gives $\epsilon_{q-1}d_j^v=F(d_j^Q)\epsilon_q$. At $p=0$ the total vertical sign is $1$. Hence $e_QD=d_Se_Q$ there. At $p=1$ the only surviving component of $e_QD$ is the horizontal one, just proved zero; for $p>1$ both sides are zero. Thus $e_Q$ is a chain map.

source.place: Tag 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution), augmentation comparisons; direct check for the displayed bar

proof.text: At $q=0$, forgetting $f$ commutes with each horizontal face: for the last face both orders delete $T_p$ and forget the composite arrow to $Q_0$, and for the first face both apply the same map of $F$. At $q=1$ the two vertical faces have exactly the same image after forgetting their final arrows, so $e_B\partial_v=0$; multiplying this zero by $(-1)^p$ has no effect. For $q>1$ neither vertical face reaches the edge $q=0$, and horizontal faces preserve $q$. These exhaust the cases in the chain-map equality, proving $e_BD=d_Be_B$.

source.place: Tag 08Q9 (lemma-compute-by-cosimplicial-resolution), edge augmentation; direct check for the displayed bar

proof.text: Fix $q$. Let $t_p$ append $Q_q\xrightarrow1Q_q$ without a sign. For $p\geq1$, the first $p+1$ faces of this appended string are $t_{p-1}d_i^h$ ($0\leq i\leq p$), and its last face is the original string. Thus $\partial_ht_p=t_{p-1}\partial_h+(-1)^{p+1}1$. Multiplication by $(-1)^{p+1}$ and the formula $h_{p-1}=(-1)^pt_{p-1}$ give $\partial_hh_p+h_{p-1}\partial_h=1$. At $p=0$, the boundary of the appended string is $(Q_q\xrightarrow1Q_q,F(f)x)-(T\xrightarrow fQ_q,x)$. Since $h_0=-t_0$, this says $\partial_hh_0=1-h_{-1}\epsilon_q$. Finally $\epsilon_qh_{-1}(y)=F(1)y=y$, proving the identity also in augmented degree $-1$. In particular, if $u\in A_{0,q}$ has $\epsilon_qu=0$ then $\partial_hh_0u=u$; if $u\in A_{p,q}$ with $p>0$ has $\partial_hu=0$, then $\partial_hh_pu=u$. These consequences will supply the lifts below.

We prove surjectivity on cohomology by a finite recursion, using homological degree $n=-r\geq0$. Let $y\in S^{-n}$ have $d_Sy=0$. Put $x_0=h_{-1}y\in A_{0,n}$. For $0\leq j<n$, having chosen $x_j\in A_{j,n-j}$, put
$$x_{j+1}=(-1)^{j+1}h_j\partial_vx_j\in A_{j+1,n-j-1}.$$
For $j=0$, $\epsilon_{n-1}\partial_vx_0=d_S\epsilon_nx_0=d_Sy=0$. For $j>0$, the induction hypothesis $\partial_hx_j=(-1)^j\partial_vx_{j-1}$ gives $\partial_h\partial_vx_j=(-1)^j\partial_v^2x_{j-1}=0$. The two lifting identities established in the preceding step therefore give $\partial_hx_{j+1}=(-1)^{j+1}\partial_vx_j$. Thus the components of $D(\sum_{j=0}^nx_j)$ cancel consecutively, and the remaining $\partial_vx_n$ is zero since its vertical degree is zero. The resulting total cycle maps to $y$. When $n=0$ this is just $x_0$ and no recursion is needed. It proves surjectivity of $H^{-n}(e_Q)$ directly from the definition of cohomology, without a total-comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), agent-written finite-diagonal dual argument with the specified augmentation

proof.text: For injectivity let $z\in(\operatorname{Tot}A)^{-n}$ be a cycle with $e_Qz=d_Sy$ for $y\in S^{-n-1}$. Regard $w_0=h_{-1}y\in A_{0,n+1}$ as a total element. Then $z'=z-Dw_0$ is a cycle whose $p=0$ component has augmentation zero. Set $r^{(0)}=z'$. Inductively suppose $r^{(k)}$ is a cycle supported in horizontal degrees $k,\ldots,n$. Its component $u_k\in A_{k,n-k}$ has augmentation zero if $k=0$; for $k>0$ its horizontal boundary is zero, since the component of $Dr^{(k)}$ in $A_{k-1,n-k}$ has no other contribution. Put $b_{k+1}=h_ku_k\in A_{k+1,n-k}$. The contraction gives $\partial_hb_{k+1}=u_k$. Subtract $Db_{k+1}$: the component in degree $k$ disappears, and the only extra component has horizontal degree $k+1$ and vertical degree $n-k-1$. The residual $r^{(k+1)}$ remains a cycle since $D^2=0$. For $k=n$ that vertical contribution is zero, so $r^{(n+1)}=0$. Hence $z=D(w_0+\sum_{k=0}^nb_{k+1})$ is a boundary. The recursion also works at $n=0$. This proves injectivity of $H^{-n}(e_Q)$.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), agent-written finite boundary elimination; verifies that the isomorphism is induced by e_Q

proof.text: The two recursions prove that $H^r(e_Q)$ is an isomorphism for every $r\leq0$. For $r>0$ both complexes have zero terms and hence zero cohomology. Thus $e_Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and localization sends this very chain map to an isomorphism in $D(R)$. No contraction of $\operatorname{Hom}(T,Q_\bullet)$ entered: the contraction used only the final arrow to the particular $Q_q$.

source.place: Tag 0133 (lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution), conclusion and identification of the displayed augmentation

proof.text: Write $D'=\partial_v+(-1)^q\partial_h$ for the transpose total differential and let $u_{p,q}=(-1)^{pq}1$. On the horizontal output $A_{p-1,q}$, $uD'$ has coefficient $(-1)^q(-1)^{(p-1)q}=(-1)^{pq}$, the coefficient of $Du$. On the vertical output $A_{p,q-1}$, its coefficient is $(-1)^{p(q-1)}=(-1)^{pq+p}$, again that of $Du$. On the axes missing components are zero. Consequently $uD'=Du$ and $u^2=1$, so $u$ is a chain isomorphism from the transpose convention to the chosen convention. On $p=0$ its coefficient is $1$, so composing with $e_Q$ gives the same edge augmentation.

There is no repair note for this item, so the 2026-10-21 re-split rule does not apply. I recomputed each step. (1) The face identities hold. (2) The cross terms of D² cancel ((-1)^p∂_h∂_v against (-1)^{p-1}∂_v∂_h), and the diagonal in degree -n has n+1 bidegrees. (3) εq∂_h vanishes on T0→T1→Q_q (F(f)F(a)x−F(fa)x=0) and ε commutes with the vertical faces, so e_Q is a chain map. (4) At q=0 forgetting f matches the bar faces, and at q=1 the two vertical faces agree, so e_B is a chain map. (5) With t_p appending 1_{Q_q}, ∂_h t_p=t_{p-1}∂_h+(-1)^{p+1}, so h_p=(-1)^{p+1}t_p is a contraction; at p=0, ∂_h h_0=1−h_{-1}ε, and εh_{-1}=1. (6) The cycle-lifting recursion x_{j+1}=(-1)^{j+1}h_j∂_v x_j is correct, with the j=0 case from d_S y=0. (7) The boundary-elimination induction is correct; at k=n the leftover term has q=-1 and vanishes. (8) The quasi-isomorphism follows from the definition. (9) The transpose signs check out: (-1)^{pq} on both horizontal and vertical outputs, and the identity on p=0. Edge cases tested: n=0, the axes, F=0, characteristic 2, a one-object category. The proof never uses representable contractibility; that hypothesis belongs to the sibling node lem-trf-two-sided-bar-contractible-augmentation.
